title: Password re-read from Keychain on every query run → repeated macOS prompts

title: Capture a real missing-index ShowPlanXML fixture (needs a scratch table)
description:
No captured fixture contains <MissingIndexes> - sys.* catalog views never produce a missing-index suggestion, and the fixtures are deliberately captured against master with sys.* objects only so no proprietary schema reaches the repo.

Consequence: the parser's MissingIndex path (billz-xi6.2) is written from the ShowPlanXML schema and covered only by a hand-authored XML const inlined in its test module - NOT a file under core/tests/fixtures/plans/, because that directory means 'captured from a real server' and a fabricated document there would fool a future reader. That test proves the parser matches what we BELIEVE the schema says; it cannot catch a wrong belief.

Unit 3's verdict logic reports missing indexes as a Problem-severity finding, so this path is load-bearing and currently unverified against reality.

TO CAPTURE: on a DEV-connected machine, create a scratch table in master or tempdb with GENERIC column names (never a tenant database, never business column names), insert enough rows that the optimizer will suggest an index, then:
  cargo run -p coot-core --example dump_plan -- missing-index "SELECT * FROM dbo.<scratch> WHERE c2 = 1"
The example forces the master context and secret-scans before writing, so it will refuse if anything sensitive appears. Drop the scratch table afterwards.
notes:
SCOPE WIDENED (billz-xi6.2 implementation, 2026-07-31): three more PlanWarning variants are parsed from the schema with no real specimen, the same honesty gap as MissingIndexes:
  - SpillToTempDb  -- capture with a large ORDER BY under a low memory grant
  - NoJoinPredicate -- capture with a CROSS JOIN / comma join with no predicate
  - UnmatchedIndex -- needs a filtered index the optimizer cannot match
NoJoinPredicate is the cheapest and most valuable: it is the accidental-cartesian signal, one of the headline ways LLM-generated SQL is wrong-but-plausible, and Unit 3 grades it Problem severity. All three can be captured against master/tempdb with generic names via the dump_plan example's ad-hoc mode, same constraints as the missing-index case.

title: Verify SET SHOWPLAN_XML ON fails loudly when the login lacks SHOWPLAN permission
description:
core/src/plan/capture.rs documents an absolute guarantee: with SHOWPLAN on, nothing in the user SQL executes, whatever it says. That guarantee holds ONLY IF run_batch(client, ctx, SHOWPLAN_ON) returns Err whenever SHOWPLAN does not actually engage. It should - denial is server error 262 and collect_multi maps errors from both query_multiple and row iteration - but nothing tests it.

BLAST RADIUS IS WHY THIS MATTERS: a later unit feeds LLM-generated SQL through this path. If the assumption is ever wrong, arbitrary generated SQL runs for real against a tenant database instead of merely being compiled. That is the one failure mode the estimated-plan design exists to make impossible.

Needs a live test with a login lacking SHOWPLAN permission (or a documented manual verification). Raised by the independent code review of billz-xi6.1; not blocking that unit because there is no evidence the assumption is currently wrong.

title: ADR-0002 misstates which executor helpers are pub(crate); audit ADRs 0002-0007 against code
description:
ADR-0002 line 41 states that connect, apply_use_statement and query_stream_to_result were all promoted to pub(crate). Only connect is; apply_use_statement (executor.rs:352) and query_stream_to_result (executor.rs:366) are private, and run_batch (executor.rs:173) was promoted instead but is not mentioned. This actively misled a teammate implementing billz-xi6.1, which is exactly what the ADR was supposed to prevent.

ROOT CAUSE: the ADR was distilled from the billz-lpb DESIGN SPEC (what was planned) rather than from the code that shipped. The implementation chose a different seam - promote the higher-level run_batch so session.rs never needs the two lower-level helpers. Both approaches are defensible; only one is true.

FIX: correct ADR-0002's Decision section to describe the actual seam. Then audit ADRs 0003-0007, which were distilled from specs the same way and carry the same risk. An ADR is trusted MORE than a spec because it claims durability, so a factual error in one is worse than the same error in a retired design doc. Landing on main as a docs commit, not inside a feature PR.
notes:
ADDITIONAL (found by the billz-xi6.1 plan review, 2026-07-31): ADR-0002 lines 59-61 say 'Two modules is still auditable; a third should require justification.' plan::capture is now that third module touching mssql_client. The ADR needs an amendment or a Related note recording the justification (design spec section 4.2: capture must own its connection so SET SHOWPLAN_XML cannot poison a reused SessionCache). billz-zlb already anticipates this.

Ground truth for the correction, verified against code: connect (executor.rs:282) and run_batch (executor.rs:173) are the pub(crate) pair; apply_use_statement (:352) and query_stream_to_result (:366) are private. session.rs:19 imports exactly {connect, run_batch}.

title: Unit 7: cross-tenant plan variance view
description: planVarianceLogic.ts (pure, bun:test) grouping outcomes into equivalence classes by plan shape, plus variance rendering in PlanPane and fan-out routing in App.svelte explain(). Serializes after Unit 6 — both touch App.svelte and PlanPane.svelte.
notes:
HANDOFF FROM billz-xi6.3's AUTHOR — invisible from the signatures, read before planning:

GROUP ON shape() DIRECTLY. Nothing else. shape() already strips the leading [Database] component from every object, which is the ONLY reason ~27 near-identical tenants collapse into a few equivalence classes instead of 27 classes of one. Any grouping that additionally compares object names - from Finding::evidence, or from PlanNode::object walked off the tree - REINTRODUCES the per-tenant split, because those two deliberately KEEP the database name (a finding's evidence should say which database; a grouping key must not).

That failure is silent and inverted: the variance view would render one class per tenant, which reads as 'every tenant has a different plan' - a plausible, alarming finding - rather than as a broken key. It was caught during Unit 3's planning only because someone traced parse.rs::object_name and noticed Database is its FIRST component.

Also: shape() keys are readable strings, not hashes. Statements are ';'-joined, siblings ','-separated, object marked by ':', a statement with no operator tree is '-', and a plan with no statements is the empty string. Longest real key measured: 965 bytes for a 32-operator plan. Fine as a HashMap key for 27 tenants.

title: Unit 3: plan verdict and shape fingerprint
description: core/src/plan/verdict.rs and fingerprint.rs. Thresholds are a hypothesis to revise after real use, not a rule engine. The fingerprint must EXCLUDE cost and row estimates: those are exactly what differs between tenants holding different data volumes, and including them would put every tenant in its own class.
notes:
HANDOFF FROM billz-xi6.2's AUTHOR (read before planning):
- PlanStatement::all_warnings() is the SINGLE entry point. Walking root's operator tree alone finds NOTHING in scan.sqlplan - all three of its warnings are statement-level, attached to QueryPlan rather than to any RelOp.
- Three of four PlanWarning variants are schema-derived with NO captured specimen (see billz-e75): NoJoinPredicate, SpillToTempDb, UnmatchedIndex. Only ImplicitConversion is fixture-backed. Treat the other three as unverified when writing verdict rules.
- convert_issue separates a blocked seek ("Seek Plan") from a merely skewed estimate ("Cardinality Estimate"). EVERYTHING captured is the latter, so grading all converts as Problem severity is a false positive on our only warning fixture.
- est_rows_read is Option<f64>; None means 'this operator does no data access', NOT 'read nothing'. It is present only on seeks and scans. est_rows_read vs est_rows is likely a better wasteful-scan signal than a raw row threshold (join node 5 returns 10 but reads 1153; scan node 11 returns 1 but reads 218).
- REQUIRED TEST (lead): assert scan.sqlplan yields an ImplicitConversion finding. This is the guard that all_warnings() is actually consulted rather than just the node tree.

title: FK graph in schema.rs: join-path generation, join linting, schema-context export

Graph algorithms are pure Rust and headless-testable. The plan XML supplies resolved join predicates, so no T-SQL parser is needed - PLAN.md section 6 deferred that as too hard.

title: App's window-level Cmd+S can stack a second NameDialog over another component's dialog
description:
Found by plan review on billz-1kn. This is a regression introduced by billz-he0's app-level Cmd+S handler.

App.svelte's onWindowKeydown guards against opening the save dialog when APP's OWN modal state is set (naming || editing !== undefined || showPrompt). It cannot see a dialog owned by any OTHER component.

Repro once billz-1kn lands a rename dialog in SavedQueryLibrary: open Rename, focus is in the rename input (not CodeMirror), press Cmd+S. CodeMirror never sees the key so defaultPrevented is false; the guard passes because App's own naming is null; saveFromEditor() runs and mounts a SECOND NameDialog at the same top:30%/left:50%/z-index:51. Both auto-focus-and-select, they overlap pixel-for-pixel, and one Escape cancels BOTH because each instance registers its own svelte:window listener.

The general fix is a shared 'is any modal open' signal that the window-level shortcut consults, rather than App enumerating the modals it happens to know about. Any future component-owned modal reintroduces this otherwise.

Scope note: App.svelte owns the handler, so this cannot be fixed from inside billz-1kn.
acceptance_criteria: A window-level shortcut cannot open a modal while any modal is open, regardless of which component owns it. Escape closes exactly one dialog. Verified with the rename dialog open and Cmd+S pressed.

title: Object tree: long table names bleed out of the sidebar instead of ellipsing
description:
Reported by Steve 2026-07-24 on real DEV data (ESP_Nomad_SE_DEV, app.Arnotts_PBI_Fact_Claims_* tables). Pre-existing, unrelated to billz-086/he0.

Long tree labels run past the sidebar and get hard-clipped mid-glyph at the aside edge. There is no ellipsis, so a truncated name gives no signal it was truncated, and two tables sharing a long prefix are indistinguishable.

Reproduced with a stubbed backend at a 320px sidebar:
- .conn-tree scrollWidth 444 vs clientWidth 319 — a 125px phantom HORIZONTAL scroll
- rows are width:100% so their boxes measure 303, but the label TEXT overflows the box
- aside overflow:hidden is what finally clips it, hence the hard cut

Cause: every tree label sets white-space:nowrap with NO overflow:hidden, NO text-overflow:ellipsis, and no min-width:0 on the flex row — so the nowrap text refuses to shrink. Affects TableNode.svelte, ViewNode.svelte, ColumnLeaf.svelte, DatabaseNode.svelte. App.svelte .conn-tree is overflow:auto, which is what turns the overflow into a horizontal scroll.

Fix direction: min-width:0 on the flex row plus overflow:hidden + text-overflow:ellipsis on the label span, in all four node components; switch .conn-tree to overflow-y:auto / overflow-x:hidden. Add a title attribute so the full name is available on hover once truncated. Roughly 6 lines of CSS plus the title.

Note the connection ROOT already does this correctly (.meta strong has nowrap+overflow:hidden) — the deeper tree nodes were never given the same treatment.
acceptance_criteria: A table/view/column name longer than the sidebar truncates with an ellipsis and exposes the full name via title on hover. .conn-tree has no horizontal scrollbar at any sidebar width. Verified light+dark with a long-named tree.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #77 — tree labels ellipse with elision-conditional titles; conn-tree horizontal scroll removed.

title: Rename a saved query in the Library
description:

Add a rename action to the Library list (inline edit or the NameDialog introduced by billz-he0 — prefer reusing NameDialog so name entry looks the same everywhere). Backend needs nothing new: save_query is an upsert by id, so renaming is a save of the same id with a new name.

title: Toast notification system (transient app-level feedback)
description:
The app has no toast/snackbar surface and no ARIA live region at all. Feedback today is either the Messages pane (a durable record of query execution), an inline banner, or nothing. Saving to the library, for example, gives zero confirmation and silently swallows errors.

Build a reusable toast system: pure toastLogic.ts (ToastKind success/error/info, addToast with oldest-eviction at MAX_TOASTS=4, dismissToast, autoDismissMs), a toasts.svelte.ts runes store owning the setTimeout map (timers cleared on manual dismiss AND on eviction so an orphan timer cannot dismiss an unrelated toast), and ToastHost.svelte mounted once in App.svelte.

Boundary that must hold: toasts are transient app-level events only. The Messages pane stays as-is for query execution output; query errors do NOT become toasts.

Design decisions (Steve, 2026-07-24): bottom-right stack; success/info auto-dismiss 4s, errors sticky until dismissed; manual close on all; kind colors reuse the existing --ok/--warn/--danger tokens (already declared light+dark in app.css); z-index 60, above the modal ladder (menus 40/41, modal 50/51) so a save failure stays visible over the dialog that caused it; CSS transitions on --dur/--ease rather than a Svelte transition directive, because app.css zeroes those tokens under prefers-reduced-motion and a JS-driven transition would bypass that guard; container aria-live=polite with role=alert on error toasts.

First consumer is billz-he0 (save-to-library confirmation).
acceptance_criteria: toastLogic.test.ts covers append order, oldest-eviction at MAX_TOASTS, dismiss by id, dismiss of unknown id is a no-op, and autoDismissMs returns null only for error. ToastHost renders a stack bottom-right with correct kind colors in light and dark. just verify passes. Light+dark screenshots of a 3-kind stack captured.
notes:
DESIGN DECISION (Steve, 2026-07-24), supersedes the original 'oldest-eviction at MAX_TOASTS=4' text in the description:

Retention and display are separate limits.
- Errors are NEVER evicted and never auto-dismiss. They accumulate without bound and leave only on explicit dismiss.
- Only MAX_VISIBLE (4) toasts render. Older ones collapse behind a '+N earlier errors' chip that expands, plus a Dismiss all control.
- Transient toasts (success/info) are still evicted oldest-first to stay within the transient budget, since they expire on their own anyway.

Rationale: kind-blind FIFO eviction contradicted the kind-aware stickiness rule — four unread errors plus one routine success silently destroyed the oldest error.

A11Y (also revised): the earlier 'container aria-live=polite with role=alert on error toasts' plan nested live regions, which double-announces on some AT and drops assertive intent on others. Replaced with two pre-mounted visually-hidden regions (polite + assertive); the visual stack carries no live-region markup and stays in the a11y tree.
close_reason: Shipped: billz-086 via PR #75 (toast system), billz-he0 via PR #76 (save-to-library push flow). Both CI-green and squash-merged to main.

title: Per-connection object state (multi-root)
description:
Replace the single shared dbStore + single ObjectTree (keyed to conns.activeId) with per-connection cached DB and tree state, so several connections can be expanded with live object trees at once.

Today: App.svelte owns one load effect → one dbStore; the tree is {#key `${conns.activeId}:${nonce}`} single-instance; the toolbar db-picker reads that one dbStore. Multi-root needs a keyed store (per connectionId) for databases and node memos, driven by which connections are expanded rather than a single activeId. Preserve the existing invariants: locked (session-only, not-unlocked) connections must not hit the DB but must still clear to empty (billz-zmw); out-of-order responses dropped; effectiveDb validation per connection.

Depends on tabs owning (connection, database) so the toolbar picker resolves against the active tab's connection's store.

title: Tabs own their (connection, database) target
description:
Foundational data-model change for multi-root. Today a query tab stores database + fanout but inherits its CONNECTION from the global conns.activeId; run() and the toolbar db-picker read conns.activeId. With N simultaneously-live connections that is a silent wrong-server hazard (same bug class the effectiveDb guard already prevents, one level up).

Make connection a tab-owned property: tab stores connectionId; run(), the toolbar (db-picker + Run + fanout), and the ParamBar path all target the tab's connection, not a global active. Handle new-tab connection defaulting and the no-connection empty state. Migrate persisted tabs in tabs.svelte (restore()) — existing tabs have no connectionId; backfill or null-with-prompt cleanly.

title: Lexer-safe @param scan (skip string literals / comments / @@ / DECLARE) — PLAN §6 prerequisite
description:
Blocks the Variables Library (billz-z6r). PARAM_RE in paramBarLogic.ts matches @word-shaped text inside string literals, -- and /* */ comments, [brackets], and DECLAREd @locals — not just real params. Today this is contained because params only derive in saved-query tabs. The moment @params derive in EVERY tab (V2's gate removal), it becomes a SILENT correctness bug:

(a) Mangled string literals: 'sales@vendor.com' derives a phantom empty @vendor; core's context-free splice_raw_text (param_bind.rs, test splice_11_context_free_inside_string_literal) turns it into 'sales.com'. Wrong rows, no error.
(b) Lost selection-run + GO-splitting: any tab containing an @token routes the WHOLE buffer through run_params; getRunTarget()'s selection/GO handling only exists on the run_sql branch.

Real fix requires a T-SQL lexer (skip strings/comments/brackets, handle prefix-colliding @cust vs @customer), which PLAN §6 explicitly DEFERS to v2 (evaluate sqlparser-rs). Shares its root cause with billz-u2t (named multi-result remap also needs this lexer). Found during independent code review of the V2 branch (spec/variables-library).

title: Results grid: header doesn't scroll horizontally with body; janky horizontal scroll
description:
Two related defects in ResultsGrid.svelte:
1. The sticky header (.header-row) is a flex sibling ABOVE the scroll container (.body), so it pins vertically (correct) but does NOT scroll horizontally with the body — scroll right and the headers stay put, misaligning from their columns.
2. Horizontal scroll is 'weird': the body's content width isn't pinned. .spacer and .tr are width:100% (of the body content box) with fixed-px grid-template-columns that overflow, and rows are position:absolute — so the horizontal scroll extent is derived from overflow rather than a defined content width, giving inconsistent scrolling.

Fix approach: give the body an explicit content width = sum of column sizes so both header and rows share one width and the horizontal scroll extent is exact; sync the header's horizontal offset to the body's scrollLeft (bind:scrollLeft) so headers track the columns. Keep the virtualizer/scroll-element wiring untouched (it is carefully tuned).
close_reason: fixed in PR #40; review nits in PR #41 (both merged to main)

title: Object tree rows render centered, not left-aligned
description:
In the Objects tree, node rows (databases/tables/views) render with their chevron+icon+label cluster centered horizontally instead of flush-left, so rows appear staggered.

Root cause: the global button base in app.css sets justify-content: center. The tree row buttons (.row in DatabaseNode/TableNode/ViewNode) override display/background/border and set text-align:left, but do NOT reset justify-content — and text-align has no effect on flex main-axis placement. So the flex items center inside the full-width (width:100%) button.

Fix: add justify-content: flex-start to .row in DatabaseNode.svelte, TableNode.svelte, ViewNode.svelte. (ColumnLeaf is an <li>, not a button — unaffected.)

title: Speed up object-tree loading — reuse the connection for schema queries (not one login per expand)
description: Expanding a DB in the object tree takes ~10s because each schema query (list_tables/list_views/list_columns via core::run) CONNECTS FRESH — a full TLS + SQL login + USE [db] per call — and a DB expand fires two (tables+views in parallel), so it pays ~two logins. The sys.* query itself is fast; the cost is the repeated login, which lands before any rows come back. FIX (high leverage): reuse a live connection for schema introspection instead of connect-per-call — a Connection wrapper owning Client<Ready> (PLAN.md §4; overlaps billz-0gh.1 connection reuse for fan-out). SchemaCache already dedups repeat expands; this targets the FIRST expand of each object. Optional/lower-payoff: incremental/streaming row delivery (executor query_stream + Tauri events) — but since the latency is upfront login, streaming would still show nothing for ~10s then everything, so connection reuse is the real win. A loading spinner (separate small change) already addresses the 'feels hung' symptom; this addresses the actual slowness.
design:
DESIGN (verified against mssql-client 0.20.2 source) — Arc<Client>+clone does NOT work.

Two independent reasons a single Client can't be Arc-shared for concurrent ops:
1. API: query_multiple(&mut self) + execute(&mut self) both take &mut self
   (client.rs:1782 / 1840). Arc<T> only yields shared &T, never &mut. And Client
   is NOT Clone (no impl) — it owns a live ConnectionHandle (TLS socket) + a
   statement cache + a transaction descriptor; nothing to cheaply clone.
2. Protocol: a TDS connection is strictly one request/response at a time (the
   Client struct even tracks "request sent, response not yet fully read" to detect
   a dirty connection). No MARS in this driver. Two ops genuinely cannot be in
   flight on one physical connection, regardless of the wrapper.

Options:
- Arc<tokio::Mutex<Client>>: reuse (skip re-login) = YES; concurrency = NO
  (serialized behind the lock). MUST be tokio::Mutex, NOT std::Mutex — the guard
  is held across .await (same guard-across-await we avoided in SchemaCache).
  RECOMMENDED starting point: smallest change, and it kills the actual cost — the
  ~10s is the LOGIN, not the query (sys.* catalog queries are milliseconds). The
  frontend Promise.all(tables, views) just queues both invokes on the lock; net
  expand time ~= one amortized login + 2 fast queries, well under 10s.
- Connection pool (N Clients via deadpool/bb8): reuse + TRUE concurrency, but more
  machinery (checkout/return, sizing, dirty-connection handling). mssql-client has
  NO built-in pool type — only instrumentation hooks (record_pool_status) for
  external pools. Only worth it if overlapping queries on ONE connection become a
  real need (e.g. two editor tabs running against the same connection at once); a
  single-user tree browser does not need it.

Recommended implementation: one lazily-connected, reused Client per connection-id,
held behind a tokio::Mutex in AppState (next to secrets/schema). Compose with the
existing SchemaCache (which already dedups repeat expands; this targets the FIRST
expand of each object).

Subtlety to preserve: a reused Client carries session state (the USE'd current
database, SET options, temp tables). run() already re-issues `USE [db]` per call
via ExecutionContext, so schema reuse stays correct — but the reuse model MUST keep
issuing that USE per call, not assume a fresh connection each time.

Start with Arc<tokio::Mutex<Client>>; upgrade to a pool only if overlapping ops
are ever actually needed.

title: Sweep comments to the global length and clarity rules
description:
The global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md now carries one set of comment and doc rules for
every project. This repo has 3 comment blocks over the ten-line cap; the longest
is 22 lines.

Find them:

```bash
find . -name '*.rs' -not -path '*/target/*' | while read -r f; do
  awk -v F="$f" '/^[ \t]*\/\// && !/^[ \t]*\/\/\// && !/^[ \t]*\/\/!/ {if(n==0)s=NR; n++; next} {if(n>10) print F":"s" ("n")"; n=0}' "$f"
done
```

The rules in short: write full sentences, never describe past behavior, rendered
docs carry the contract while body comments carry the design, no plain comment
block over ten lines, and zero docs beat docs that confuse.

Trimming a block means keeping the constraint it records and dropping the
argument for it. Relocate rather than delete when a comment names a trap.

title: Revisit the verdict thresholds after first real use against LLM-generated SQL
description:
The four verdict constants in core/src/plan/verdict.rs (LARGE_SCAN_ROWS_READ=100_000, WASTEFUL_READ_RATIO=100, EXPENSIVE_COST=10.0, MISSING_INDEX_IMPACT=50.0) are a HYPOTHESIS, per the plan-verdict design spec section 6, not a calibrated design.

None of them is exercised by real data. Every captured fixture is a sys.* metadata query against master, so the corpus tops out at 25871 rows read and 0.75402 total cost, and contains zero missing indexes. All three numeric thresholds sit above everything we have. They are covered by synthetic boundary tests plus a negative sweep proving no real fixture trips them - honest, but it means the rules are calibrated on judgment rather than evidence.

MISSING_INDEX_IMPACT is the one expected to move first; it may well want to be 0, since the server only emits a missing-index group when it already thinks the index matters.

REVISIT after the tool has been pointed at real bot-generated SQL against real tenant databases, which is the whole point of the feature. Resist making these configurable - spec section 6 explicitly forbids a rule engine, and a configurable threshold is harder to change than a constant while still having guessed.

title: capture_xml returns only the first plan document; GO-split SQL is silently lossy
description:
core/src/plan/capture.rs first_xml_cell scans the returned result sets and returns the FIRST non-empty XML/Text cell. SHOWPLAN_XML emits one document per BATCH, so a single batch containing several statements is fine (verified: two-statements.sqlplan carries 2 StmtSimple elements in one document). But GO-split SQL sends multiple batches, and every document after the first is silently discarded.

Not reachable today - the explain commands send only the first resolved batch (see the Tauri command in the plan-verdict work). It becomes reachable the moment multi-batch explain is wanted.

The behaviour is correctly documented in first_xml_cell's doc comment, but that note had no bead reference, so it was at risk of rotting. Raised by the independent plan review of billz-xi6.2. Reference this bead from that comment when the file is next touched.

The differentiated surface is explain_across_tenants, lint_join_paths, compare_results, so the analyses must exist in core first; building the server before them yields a commodity. Composes with a Langfuse MCP server so an agent moves trace data between the two without Coot ever integrating Langfuse. core being Tauri-free already makes a headless MCP binary a new crate rather than a refactor - relevant if a teammate working in Vertex ever needs it without a desktop app. Must respect the invariant: mssql-client types still never escape core.

title: Langfuse corpus replay: batch-judge logged bot queries
description: The rate lever on the bot's retry latency. Replay a corpus of bot-generated queries as estimated plans across tenants, cluster by problem class, rank worst offenders. One-at-a-time inspection tells you this query is bad; the corpus tells you the bot always fans out before aggregating - one prompt fix that removes a whole retry category. INGEST VIA EXPORTED FILE, not a Langfuse HTTP client: keeps Coot's outbound network surface at zero (SQL Server only today) and avoids storing a second credential. Wait until the interactive verdict has been used by hand for a while - batch-computing the wrong verdict across hundreds of traces is worse than not computing it.

title: Library panel has no reload path and cannot distinguish empty from failed
description:
Found by billz-rvg's plan review.

Two related gaps in the saved-query Library panel:

1. refreshLibrary() at App.svelte:518 is the only explicit library load, and there is no Refresh affordance in LibraryPanel.svelte or SavedQueryLibrary.svelte. If that launch load fails, the Library stays empty until the app is restarted. billz-rvg adds a toast reporting the failure — but reports a state the user cannot recover from in-app.

2. On failure library.list stays [] and the panel renders 'No saved queries yet.' — an affirmative statement that the user has no saved queries, which is a lie about their data. After the rvg toast is dismissed, that lie is all that remains on screen.

Note an incidental recovery path exists and is worse than none: save() and remove() call refresh() internally, so saving a query while the read-back is still failing can leave the panel showing ONLY the newly-saved row.

Proper fix is a load status on the store, mirroring databases.svelte.ts's DbEntry (idle/loading/loaded/error), rendered as a distinct error state with a retry — which also gives the panel the Refresh affordance it lacks. Contrast with the object tree, which already does exactly this and is why rvg correctly leaves DB-list errors alone.
acceptance_criteria: A failed library load renders a distinct error state with a retry affordance, never 'No saved queries yet.' The panel can be reloaded without restarting the app.
notes:
CORRECTION (lead, after billz-rvg's implementation): the 'incidental recovery path' framing in the description above is WRONG, and it was my error — I wrote it into this bead from rvg's plan and endorsed it at the plan gate.

The claimed degenerate case (a save while the read-back still fails leaving the panel showing ONLY the newly-written row) is NOT REACHABLE. QueryStore::upsert opens with self.list()? at core/src/query_store.rs:59, so anything that breaks list_queries breaks save_query FIRST. This is precisely the argument billz-sjn's own comment makes about why swallowing its refresh error is safe — the same mechanism, two files away, and neither rvg nor I connected them until rvg re-read the store mid-implementation.

The honest framing, which reaches the same conclusion by a cleaner route: a steady-state read failure leaves the library empty until relaunch, with no in-app recovery, because there is NO self-repair path at all. That strengthens the case for a Refresh affordance rather than weakening it.

The two real gaps stand unchanged: (1) no reload path short of restarting; (2) the panel renders 'No saved queries yet.' on a failed load, which is an affirmative lie about the user's data.

title: connections.svelte.ts save()/remove() have the same refresh-failure bug as savedQueries
description:
Found by code review on billz-sjn. Same bug class, different store, no existing bead.

connections.svelte.ts save() is 'await saveConnection(cfg, password); await refresh();' and remove() is the same shape. A failed list_connections is indistinguishable from a failed save_connection, so a successful write followed by a failed read-back reports as a failed save and leaves the list stale — exactly what billz-sjn fixed for saved queries.

Less severe than the query case: ConnectionForm mints the id once, so a retry upserts rather than minting a duplicate row. But the stale-list half is identical.

IMPORTANT — the fix is NOT a copy-paste of sjn's. conns.remove() also performs activeId nulling, dropDatabases and pruneRoot, and those must stay correctly ordered relative to any local mirror update. Verify connection_store's upsert has the same read-then-write structure that makes swallowing the refresh error safe in the saved-query case (that shared read path is the whole justification), rather than assuming it does.
acceptance_criteria: A successful connection write followed by a failed refresh does not report as a failed save and does not leave conns.list stale. remove()'s activeId/dropDatabases/pruneRoot sequencing is preserved.
notes:
SHARPENED by billz-rvg's code review — the user-visible consequence is now concrete, not theoretical.

billz-rvg adds an error toast to ConnectionNode's delete. Because connections.svelte.ts:34 is a bare 'await refresh()', a failed READ-BACK rejects remove() AFTER the delete has already committed. So the new toast says 'Couldn't delete "X"' for a connection that IS deleted, and leaves a stale row in the sidebar.

Before rvg this path was silent (no catch at all), so the bug existed but said nothing. Now it makes an affirmative false statement — which is worse, and is the same reason billz-sjn's fix mattered on the library side.

The asymmetry is now visible in the code: SavedQueryLibrary's delete comment can honestly say 'since billz-sjn a throw from the store means the WRITE failed', while ConnectionNode's cannot. rvg's comment was narrowed to name that gap and cite this bead.

Fix is ~3 lines mirroring savedQueries.svelte.ts:62-66 (try/catch + console.warn around the re-read), plus the local mirror. Still NOT a copy-paste: conns.remove() also does activeId nulling, dropDatabases and pruneRoot, which must stay ordered relative to the mirror update. Also confirm connection_store's upsert has the same read-then-write structure that makes swallowing the refresh error safe for saved queries.

title: Bare-await save/remove sites in App.svelte and SavedQueryLibrary have no error handling
description:
Split out of billz-sjn's plan to keep that diff about the save() contract alone. Natural home is billz-rvg (migrate remaining feedback surfaces to toasts).

App.svelte's onScopeChange and onTypeChange await save() with NO try/catch. A genuine WRITE failure there is an unhandled promise rejection with zero user feedback — the param's scope or type silently fails to persist and the UI shows the change as if it stuck.

billz-sjn does NOT fix this. sjn fixes the refresh-failure half (a failed read-back no longer rejects, so the stale-params symptom in billz-ivb goes away), but a real write failure still throws into nothing. Roughly 3 lines each: try/catch to a pushToast error.

Worth doing with rvg since that unit is already routing feedback surfaces to toasts and is the next one up.
acceptance_criteria: A write failure in onScopeChange or onTypeChange surfaces to the user rather than becoming an unhandled rejection.
notes:
WIDENED after billz-sjn's code review: onDelete is a THIRD site and was recorded nowhere.

SavedQueryLibrary.svelte onDelete awaits remove(q.id) with no try/catch. billz-sjn improved it (a failed read-back no longer throws while leaving the deleted row on screen), but a genuine DELETE failure is still an unhandled rejection with zero user feedback.

Full list of bare-await sites after sjn:
- App.svelte onScopeChange  — write failure silent
- App.svelte onTypeChange   — write failure silent
- SavedQueryLibrary onDelete — delete failure silent

All three are ~3 lines of try/catch to a pushToast error, and all three belong with billz-rvg.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #81 (folded into billz-rvg). All three bare-await sites now surface write failures; the scope/type selects also revert their DOM value, since no reactive-only fix works.

title: onScopeChange/onTypeChange show stale params when save()'s refresh fails
description:
Found by billz-1kn's author while implementing; adjacent to billz-sjn's area.

App.svelte's param-persistence paths (around the onScopeChange / onTypeChange / run-time persistDeclared call sites) invoke saveQuery from lib/api directly rather than going through savedQueries.svelte's save(). The store's save() is saveQuery-then-refresh; calling the raw command skips the refresh, so library.list keeps the pre-write params until something else happens to refresh it.

Consequence: the Library panel and anything deriving from library.list (curSavedQuery, and therefore the param bar) can show stale param config after a scope or type change until an unrelated refresh occurs.

Sequencing note: billz-sjn is already reworking what save() promises across its five callers. These direct-call sites are effectively a sixth and seventh caller that opted out of the contract entirely, so sjn should decide whether they route through save() or stay raw deliberately.
acceptance_criteria: Param-persistence writes either route through the store's save() or are documented as deliberately raw with the staleness accepted. The Library panel does not show stale params after a scope or type change.
notes:
CORRECTION (2026-07-27, lead): the original title and description were WRONG about the mechanism. Verified exhaustively:

  grep across app/ui/src shows lib/savedQueries.svelte.ts is the ONLY importer of the raw saveQuery/deleteQuery/listQueries commands from ./api. App.svelte line 22 imports 'save as saveQuery' from the STORE. So its call sites at 197/250/306/315 all go through save(); there is no bypass and never was. The 'sixth and seventh caller that opted out of the contract' framing was my error, formed from the alias name without checking the import.

The SYMPTOM is real and correctly observed. The actual mechanism: save() is saveQuery-then-refresh, and refresh()'s rejection propagates out of save(). onScopeChange/onTypeChange have no try/catch, so a failed read-back becomes an unhandled rejection AND leaves library.list holding pre-write params — the panel and param bar then show stale scope/type config.

That makes this a symptom of billz-sjn, not an independent bug. billz-sjn's fix (update library.list locally from the write, treat refresh as best-effort reconciliation) resolves it directly. Close as fixed-by-sjn once that lands, rather than fixing separately.

Credit: caught by billz-sjn's author during plan-phase exploration, which is exactly what the plan gate is for.
close_reason: Fixed by billz-sjn (PR #80). Its original diagnosis was wrong — App.svelte imports save as saveQuery from the STORE, not the raw command, so no bypass ever existed. The stale-params symptom was this bug reaching onScopeChange/onTypeChange, and sjn's local mirror update resolves it.

title: Live-region announcer misses a repeat when the string already equals what the region holds
description:
Surfaced properly during billz-667 plan review. Pre-existing; billz-667 NARROWS this but does not close it, and its comment now says so honestly rather than claiming a fix.

toasts.svelte.ts keeps one string per politeness (announcer.polite / announcer.assertive). A live region only re-announces on a DOM change, so any push whose announcement text EQUALS what that region already holds is silent for screen-reader users. billz-667's repeat count fixes only the sub-case where the previous instance is still the newest toast (the count makes the string differ).

Three live cases remain:
1. Push a success, let it auto-dismiss after 4s, push the identical string — stack empty or newest differs, so no coalesce, bare text, region unchanged. Silent.
2. Dismiss an error via its close button, then the identical error recurs — dismiss() does not clear the announcer (only dismissAll does), so the region still holds that string. Silent.
3. Two identical messages separated only by a message of the OTHER politeness (success X, error Y, success X) — the two regions are independent fields, so .polite never changed. Silent.

Fix direction: make the region's content change unconditionally per push — either append an invisible nonce, or clear the field then set it on the next microtask/tick so the mutation is observable. Whichever, it must not double-announce.

Sighted users see every one of these (a new toast, or a badge ticking up); AT users do not. That asymmetry is the bug.
acceptance_criteria: An identical message pushed after the previous instance left the stack, after being dismissed, or interleaved with the other politeness, is announced each time. No double-announcement in the normal case. Verified against the two pre-mounted regions.
notes:
Fourth residual case, found by code review on billz-667 (not in the original description):

4. Two adjacent identical texts of DIFFERENT kinds within the SAME politeness group — e.g. success 'X' then info 'X'. The kinds differ so coalescing correctly declines to merge them, but both write the bare string 'X' to announcer.polite, so the second is silent.

Not reachable from today's call sites (App.svelte only pushes success and error, which sit in different politeness groups), but it is reachable the moment any caller pushes an info toast whose text matches a recent success. Whatever fix lands must cover it — a nonce or clear-then-set approach does so automatically, which is another argument for that shape over special-casing the coalescing path.

title: save() reports a refresh failure as a save failure, orphaning the row
description:
Found by code review on billz-he0.

savedQueries.svelte.ts save() awaits saveQuery(q) then refresh(). If the write SUCCEEDS but the follow-up listQueries() fails (connection drop between the two invokes), the rejection propagates from refresh, so every caller treats it as a failed save.

Concretely in saveToLibrary: the catch fires, the toast says the save failed, and setTabSavedQuery is skipped — so the tab stays scratch. But the row IS persisted. The user retries and gets a SECOND row with the same name and a fresh UUID: exactly the duplicate-entry class of bug billz-he0 set out to eliminate, reintroduced through the error path.

Not fixed in he0 because the fix belongs in save() and changes error semantics for all five callers (promote, update, param scope change, param type change, run-time param persistence). Needs a deliberate decision about what save() promises: probably that a write failure and a read-back failure are DIFFERENT outcomes, with only the former meaning 'your data was not saved'.
acceptance_criteria: A successful write followed by a failed refresh does not report the save as failed and does not leave the tab unlinked. Callers can distinguish write failure from read-back failure.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #80 — save() throws only on write failure; library.list updated from the write; refresh is best-effort reconciliation. Rust tripwire added for in-place upsert ordering.

title: Toasts: coalesce repeated identical messages
description:
Found by code review on billz-086.

pushToast mints a fresh crypto.randomUUID() every call, so nothing coalesces. A failure that repeats on a timer — a background refresh or reconnect against a down DEV box — pushes a new sticky error toast per tick. After MAX_TOASTS ticks the stack is N identical never-expiring copies of the same message, and every later toast of any kind is evicted on arrival. The user has to click the close button once per copy.

Fix direction: on push, if the newest toast has the same kind and text, bump a repeat count on it (and reset its timer if non-sticky) instead of appending. Rendering the count as a small 'x3' badge keeps it honest — silently dropping repeats would hide that the failure is recurring, which is information.

Depends on the eviction-policy decision in billz-086; do that first.
acceptance_criteria: A message pushed N times in a row occupies one slot showing a repeat count. Non-sticky repeats reset their timer. Distinct messages still stack normally. Covered in toastLogic.test.ts.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #78 — repeated identical toasts coalesce into one counted slot; count rides the screen-reader announcement. Residual announcer gap tracked as billz-b8f.

title: Connection row hover highlight excludes the chevron; active highlight does not
description:
Visual inconsistency in the sidebar connection roots (fallout from billz-a5y.4/a5y.8), spotted by Steve 2026-07-24.

The ACTIVE root highlight is on the li: li.active spans the full row, 8px to 311px, including the chevron column, plus the 2px inset accent marker.

The HOVER highlight is on the .name button instead: .name:hover starts at 39px, AFTER the chevron, and ends at 305px. So hovering carves the chevron column out of the highlight while the active state includes it. Two states, two different boxes, stacked in the same list — the chevron sits on bare background inside an otherwise highlighted row, which reads as an unexplained vertical gutter.

Measured in Chrome at a 320px sidebar: li 8-311, .name 39-305. Reproduced in both themes.

Fix is to move the hover tint from .name to .root-row (or the li) so hover and active share one box. Watch that .twisty:hover and .name:hover do not then double-tint, and that the a5y.8 mask-based name fade still lines up.
acceptance_criteria: Hover and active highlights occupy the same box on a connection root in both themes. No double-tinting when hovering the chevron specifically. Verified with light+dark screenshots.

title: Migrate remaining feedback surfaces to toasts
description:
Follow-on to billz-086 (toast system) and billz-he0. Deliberately out of scope of he0 to keep that PR reviewable.

Surfaces still using ad-hoc or no feedback:
- App.svelte library refresh seeds with a bare catch that swallows the error entirely — a silent failure.
- Connection failures / unlock errors.
- SavedQueryLibrary delete uses the native confirm() dialog.

Reroute these to the toast system where they are transient app events. Do NOT move query-execution output out of the Messages pane — that boundary is intentional.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #81 — seven feedback surfaces routed to toasts, nine deliberately left alone with reasoning recorded.

title: Extract shared ContextMenu.svelte; migrate TableNode + ConnectionNode
description: After billz-a5y.4, two inline context menus exist: TableNode's (scoped-query, cursor-only) and ConnectionNode's (Edit/Delete, with button-anchored open, focus return, viewport clamp, role=menu). .4 deliberately reuse-inlined ConnectionNode's menu (mirroring TableNode's pattern) to avoid destabilizing the working TableNode menu. Follow-on: extract a small shared ContextMenu.svelte (backdrop, Escape, positioning via clampMenuPosition, role=menu/menuitem, focus management) and migrate BOTH TableNode and ConnectionNode onto it, keeping each menu's behavior identical. A // TODO in ConnectionNode.svelte points here. Good candidate to fold into the billz-a5y.8 visual/polish pass or do standalone.

title: remove() should null-out tabs referencing a deleted connection
description: Follow-on from billz-a5y.1 (tab-owned connection). remove() nulls conns.activeId directly but cannot clear OTHER tabs' connectionId without creating a tabs<->connections import cycle. As of .1 all readers degrade gracefully on a dangling (deleted) connectionId — run() nudges, the db-picker is disabled, ObjectTree presence-gates to empty state (the code-review --fix caught a stuck-spinner here) — so there is no user-visible defect today. But the stale tab.connectionId persists until the user re-selects. Proper fix: an inversion or event seam (e.g. connections emits a 'removed' event that tabs subscribes to) to null out referencing tabs' connectionId on delete, without the direct import cycle. Deferred polish; not required for correctness.

title: Skip DECLARE'd @locals from @param detection (semantic, follow-on to billz-7c9)
description: billz-7c9 made @param scanning lexer-safe (skips strings/comments/brackets/@@). A DECLARE'd @local (DECLARE @x INT; ... @x) is in NORMAL SQL context, so the lexer correctly still sees it as a @name — it surfaces as one harmless, unset param field in the bar. Suppressing it requires statement-level SEMANTIC parsing (recognize DECLARE, parse the declaration list, exclude those names), a different axis than lexical scanning and deliberately out of 7c9's scope. Low harm today: if the user doesn't fill the field, splice_raw_text leaves it literal (splice_8) and the DECLARE runs fine. Build only if it becomes annoying.

title: Disable spellcheck on the username connection field
description: The username input in the connection form gets a red squiggly spell-check underline (browser default on text inputs). Turn it off: set spellcheck="false" (and likely autocorrect/autocapitalize off) on the username field so identifiers aren't flagged as misspellings. Small frontend polish.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #64 (5517e99): spellcheck/autocorrect off on username/server/default-db fields.

title: Decide + set Content-Security-Policy (tauri.conf.json csp is null)
description: app/tauri.conf.json sets security.csp = null, disabling CSP. Practical risk today is low (Svelte auto-escapes, zero {@html} sinks, capabilities grant no shell/fs/http), but it removes defense-in-depth for any future {@html} or dependency-injected markup in a webview that renders untrusted SQL result data. Set a restrictive CSP or record the deliberate decision to leave it off.
acceptance_criteria: Either set a restrictive CSP in tauri.conf.json (e.g. default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self' ipc: http://ipc.localhost — verifying CodeMirror/Svelte injected styles and Tauri v2 IPC still work), or add a code comment/bead documenting the conscious choice to keep csp null.
notes: Surfaced by release-readiness security audit. Non-blocking for v0.1.0; cheap to close the category.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #60 (merged 147cd98): dbStore-clear fix + restrictive CSP

title: Parameterized fan-out — bind @params across tenant DBs
description: Deferred from fan-out UI (PR#2). Today fan-out runs RAW batch text (plain run_sql analog); the fan-out toggle is gated OFF on saved-query tabs that have active @params, since run_fanout (Unit 1/2) only runs plain batches — no bind-param path. To support fanning a PARAMETERIZED saved query across tenants, run_fanout/run_params would need a bound-params variant (run_fanout_with_params) and the UI toggle would need to allow param tabs. Flagged by plan-reviewer-ui-r1.

title: Persist result-grid column widths across result-set switches / sessions
description: Follow-up to billz-a4e (drag-to-resize shipped in PR #45). Column widths currently live in table-core's columnSizing state INSIDE ResultsGrid.svelte, and ResultTabs.svelte wraps the grid in {#key selectedResult}, so switching result sets remounts the grid and resets widths to the 160px default. Persist widths so a resized column stays sized. Design question: key the widths by WHAT? Options — (a) per column-name signature of the result set (survives re-runs of the same query shape), (b) per saved-query id, (c) session-only in-memory map lifted above the {#key}. Mirror the localStorage keyed-Record pattern in globalParams.svelte.ts (load-on-init, merge-and-persist-on-write, quiet degrade on corrupt/quota). Lifting sizing state above the {#key} remount is the core structural change.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #53 (column width persistence)

title: Double-click a column resize handle to autofit width
description: Follow-up to billz-a4e (drag-to-resize shipped in PR #45). Double-clicking a column's .resizer handle in ResultsGrid.svelte should autofit the column to its content (widest visible cell + header, clamped to minSize 56). table-core has no built-in autofit — measure text width for the header label + the visible rows' rendered text (renderCell output) and call column.getResizeHandler()'s underlying setColumnSizing, or set the size directly via table.setColumnSizing({[colId]: fitWidth}). Wire ondblclick on the existing .resizer div. Consider measuring against only the virtualized/visible rows (cheap) vs a canvas measureText pass over all rows (accurate but O(rows)). UX: also useful as a per-column 'reset to fit'.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #54 (double-click autofit column width)

title: Resizable table-result columns (drag handles in ResultsGrid header)
description: Let me drag a column border in the results grid to widen/narrow it. Currently ResultsGrid.svelte (app/ui/src/lib/) sizes each column from table-core's header.getSize()/cell.column.getSize() and pins the header+body to a computed totalWidth/gridTemplate — but sizes are fixed at render. TanStack table-core already supports this: enable columnResizing (enableColumnResizing, columnResizeMode: 'onChange'), render a drag handle per <th> wired to header.getResizeHandler(), and drive the existing gridTemplate/totalWidth from the live sizing state so header + virtualized body stay in sync. Nice-to-haves (defer if they add scope): double-click a handle to autofit, and persist widths per result/column.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #45: drag-to-resize result grid columns (table-core resizing + reactive width snapshot; verified live drag, minSize floor, light+dark)

title: glib advisory (RUSTSEC VariantStrIter) — revisit when Tauri Linux backend moves to gtk4
description:
Track the medium-severity glib unsoundness advisory (VariantStrIter Iterator impls, vulnerable <0.20.0). It is NOT fixable today and this is upstream-blocked, not macOS-only:

- glib is now at 0.22.8, fix landed in 0.20.0. BUT gtk3-rs (crate 'gtk') is frozen at 0.18.2 (terminal gtk3 release) and pins glib ^0.18.
- Tauri's Linux webview stack — tao 0.35.3 + wry 0.55.1 (both LATEST) — still uses gtk3 + webkit2gtk, pulling gtk 0.18.2 → glib 0.18.5. tauri 2.11.5 is also latest. So glib 0.18 is current across the entire chain; there is no version to bump to.
- Getting glib >=0.20 requires Tauri/wry/tao to migrate the Linux backend from gtk3/webkit2gtk to gtk4/webkitgtk-6.0 — a large upstream migration not yet shipped. Fixing it ourselves = forking wry/tao (out of scope, 'crazy huge effort').

Cross-platform note (per user): Linux builds STILL WORK on glib 0.18 — this is a low-practical-risk unsoundness in GVariant string-array iteration, internal to the GTK backend. Keep Linux viable; change nothing that breaks it.

Unblock trigger: watch tao/wry release notes for a gtk4/webkitgtk-6.0 backend. When shipped, bump tauri/wry, re-run 'cargo tree -i glib', confirm >=0.20, and clear the advisory.

If a local 'cargo audit'/'cargo deny' gate is ever added, add an ignore entry for this RUSTSEC id with a pointer to this bead so CI doesn't fail on an unfixable transitive dep.
notes: Handled 2026-07-13 (option C): Dependabot alert #1 dismissed (tolerable_risk); cargo-deny config added in PR #43 (deny.toml ignores RUSTSEC-2024-0429 + unmaintained=workspace to drop the transitive gtk3 cluster; 'just audit' recipe). This bead stays open as the REVISIT tracker: when tao/wry ship a gtk4/webkitgtk-6.0 Linux backend, bump tauri, confirm 'cargo tree -i glib' shows >=0.20, then remove the RUSTSEC-2024-0429 ignore from deny.toml.

title: TypeScript 7 upgrade — blocked on svelte-check support
description:
typescript 7.0.2 (the native/Go port) is available but NOT adoptable yet: it changed the npm package's export shape, so svelte-check crashes at startup — 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading useCaseSensitiveFileNames)' because svelte-check reads typescript.default.sys, which is undefined under TS7. Vite/rolldown builds fine (doesn't use the TS API that way), but just ui-check / just verify would be permanently red.

Held at typescript ^6 (latest svelte-check supports). Revisit when svelte-check ships TS7 compatibility, then bump typescript to ^7 and confirm 'just ui-check' passes. From the billz-71r deps update, 2026-07-13.
notes: Confirmed 2026-07-13: svelte-check 4.7.2 is the LATEST release; its peerDependency is typescript>=5.0.0 (no upper bound), so it *claims* TS7 support but crashes at startup under typescript 7.0.2 (reads typescript.default.sys → undefined). typescript dist-tags: latest=7.0.2, next=7.1.0-dev, so 7.x is the current major and 6.x is prior-major (we hold at ^6). No svelte-check workaround exists — tsc alone can't typecheck .svelte templates. Unblock trigger: a svelte-check release that runs under TS7. Then bump typescript to ^7 and confirm 'just ui-check'.

title: Update all dependencies — minor and major versions
description:
Bring all deps current across the workspace — Rust (Cargo) and frontend (bun/app/ui) — including MAJOR version bumps, not just minor/patch. Motivated in part by a GitHub Dependabot advisory (1 moderate) on the default branch.

Scope:
- Rust: cargo update for minor; review + bump major versions in core/ and app/ Cargo.toml (cargo add pulls latest per CLAUDE.md). Commit Cargo.lock.
- Frontend: bun update / bun add latest for app/ui deps (Svelte 5, Vite, CodeMirror 6, TanStack Table/Virtual). Commit bun.lock.
- CRITICAL per CLAUDE.md: after any mssql-client bump, re-run the spike integration tests (just probe-typed / probe-dynamic, env-gated) before trusting the driver — it is fast-moving, single-maintainer. Stop and report if smoke tests fail, do not paper over.
- Run 'just verify' (full Rust+frontend gate); cargo fmt + clippy clean (warnings are errors).
- Watch for breaking changes on major bumps; note any that require code changes or that we choose to pin.

title: Tree-row selection highlight in the object tree
description: Follow-up to the UI refresh (billz-xhv). The design called for a 'selected row' highlight in the object tree (accent-tinted background on the active node, per the capstone mockup), but the tree currently has NO selection concept — only expand/collapse (DatabaseNode/TableNode/ViewNode/ColumnLeaf under lib/tree/). Add a selected-node state (e.g. the last-clicked node id, held in a small store or ObjectTree) and wire the '.selected' styling that Phase B already anticipated (accent-tinted bg + accent-press text). Deferred from the refresh because it required new state, out of scope for a presentational pass.
