Gates green, final review PASS, visually verified light+dark.

title: Per-tab dirty indicator dot in TabBar
description: Follow-up to the UI refresh (billz-xhv). The design called for a dirty-indicator dot on each editor tab, but it wasn't built: 'dirty' is only computed for the ACTIVE saved-query tab (App.svelte ~line 120, comparing curTab.content to curSavedQuery.sql), and QueryTab (tabsLogic.ts) has no per-tab dirty field. To show a dot per tab, compute per-tab dirtiness (each tab's content vs its linked saved query's stored SQL; non-saved-query tabs are never dirty) and render an accent dot in TabBar. Small state addition; presentational payoff. Deferred from the refresh because building it during a styling pass would have meant inventing state (out of scope then).
close_reason: Shipped in PR #50 (per-tab dirty dot)

title: Deferred: manual light/dark theme toggle UI
description: Follow-up to the UI refresh: add an explicit in-app light/dark toggle that stamps data-theme (the attribute hook already exists from Phase A). Deferred from v1, which is OS-follow only. Single-user tool — nice-to-have.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #52 (light/dark/system theme toggle)

title: Explicit "Update saved query" action in the library
description: Complement to d28.8's stable-template decision: since Run never persists SQL edits back to a saved query (edits are scratch), there is no way to update an existing saved query's SQL/params in place — 'Promote current tab' only creates a NEW entry (new UUID). Add a deliberate 'Update saved query' action (button in SavedQueryLibrary, or save-back on the opened tab) that writes curTab.content + declared params to the linked saved query (curTab.savedQueryId). This is the explicit, non-silent counterpart to the rejected 'Run = save' option (d28.8 option a). Out of scope for d28.8; filed per that brainstorm.
acceptance_criteria: An opened saved query can be updated in place (sql + params) via a deliberate user action, distinct from Promote (which creates new); linked tab reflects the update.
close_reason: Explicit Update saved query button (PR #32). Toolbar button next to Run, enabled only when curTab.content diverges from curSavedQuery.sql; writes sql + deriveParams-reconciled params in place (targetDatabase + values untouched). Completes d28.8's Run-vs-Update pair.

title: Decide edit-and-run persistence for opened saved queries
description: d28.3 code-review edge (F1): opening a saved query into a tab makes the SQL editable, but run() persists rememberValues(curParams,…) — params derived from the EDITED content — against curSavedQuery with its UNCHANGED sql. So editing a saved query's SQL and running can leave the stored sql and params inconsistent: reopening derives params from the old sql (dropping a remembered value for an edited-in @param, or leaving orphan params in storage). Non-crashing cruft; the common flow (open unchanged, fill, run) is unaffected. Resolve the semantics: either (a) run also persists sql: curTab.content (run = save edits — but a silent write), or (b) remember values only for params declared in the saved query (edits stay scratch). Pick one when the param-declaration UX matures (d28.5/d28.7).
acceptance_criteria: Opened-then-edited saved query has consistent stored sql+params after run; documented behavior.
close_reason: Saved query = stable template (PR #31). persistDeclared remembers only stored-sql params; edited-in params + SQL edits are scratch, edit-out non-destructive. Stored sql/params consistent by construction. Explicit save-back filed as d28.10.

title: Classify transient vs deterministic errors so introspection retry is precise
description: SessionCache::run retries once on a reused client for ANY error. That heals a stale socket, but a deterministic failure on a warm connection (offline DB, permission denied) still triggers a wasted reconnect+relogin and can mask the true cause if the reconnect itself hits a transient fault. Precise behavior needs distinguishing transport/connection errors (retry) from server/query errors (surface immediately) — but core stringifies driver errors into CoreError::Query, so there's no structured kind to branch on today. Fix: add a transport-vs-server error kind at the executor boundary, then retry only on transport. Deferred by the billz-lpb spec ('distinguishing is hard at the stringified boundary'); surfaced repeatedly in the high review. Low-frequency on a single-user tool (offline DBs are greyed; you have perms on your own DEV DBs).
acceptance_criteria: Retry fires only for transport/connection errors; a deterministic server error (offline/permission) is surfaced on the first attempt with no second login.
close_reason: Retry only on transport errors (CoreError::Transport + map_driver_error classifier); classification verified vs driver + unit-tested. Agent-reviewed, gates green, merged PR #26.

title: Share one databases store between ObjectTree and the DB picker
description: cwt.9 added a second list_databases loader in App.svelte for the DB picker; ObjectTree.svelte has its own. Two IPC round-trips per connection-switch/Refresh and two DatabaseInfo lists that could drift if one loader changes. Extract a shared databases.svelte.ts store (mirroring connections.svelte.ts / savedQueries.svelte.ts) consumed by both. Low harm today (both hit the same cached schema.rs), so deferred from the cwt.9 review rather than done inline. Source: xhigh code-review finding on PR #20.
acceptance_criteria: One databases store; ObjectTree and the picker both read it; a single list_databases call per connection/Refresh.
close_reason: Shared databases.svelte.ts store; single load trigger, race guard, tree+picker consistent. Agent-reviewed LGTM, gates green, merged PR #25.

title: Parameterized (named-bind) query returns only the first result set
description: mssql-client 0.20.2 has no query_multiple_named: query_named returns a single QueryStream, and the multi-result path (query_multiple -> into_query_streams) only accepts POSITIONAL params (auto-named @p1,@p2...). The RPC builders (convert_named_params etc.) are pub(crate), so we can't build a named multi-result RPC ourselves. Consequence in run_with_params (d28.2): a query that carries NAMED bind params (@cust) returns only its first result set; a query with only raw-text params or none still goes through query_multiple and preserves multi-result. Fine for 'good enough for me' — genuine parameterized filter queries are single-statement. ESCAPE HATCH if ever needed (verified cheap, not a rewrite): rewrite the user's @cust -> @p1 positionally and route through query_multiple (positional non-empty params ALSO emit sp_executesql, client.rs:1809-1812), remapping names back for display. Only build this if a real multi-statement parameterized query need appears. Source: mssql-client-0.20.2 client.rs:1047-1078 (query_named), stream.rs:733 (into_query_streams).
notes: FEASIBILITY (batch review): the ONLY multi-result path is query_multiple, which takes POSITIONAL params named @p1..@pN (driver client.rs:706); the user writes @named, so this needs rewriting @cust -> @p1 in the SQL TEXT. Doing that safely (skip string literals, -- and /* */ comments, [bracketed] idents, prefix-colliding names like @cust vs @customer) requires a T-SQL lexer, which PLAN.md §6 explicitly DEFERS (statement-precision/lexing = v2, evaluate sqlparser-rs later). A naive regex remap would corrupt @params inside strings/comments — a safety regression the bind path must not have. The current query_named single-result behavior is safe and correct. DEFER until the §6 lexer lands, then route bind params through query_multiple with a lexer-safe remap. (Deeper look reversed the initial shallow 'feasible' call — the positional API exists, but a safe remap does not without lexing.)

title: Stale edit-form after deleting the connection being edited
description: In the connection manager (cwt.3), deleting a connection from the list while its edit form is open leaves App.svelte's  state holding the now-deleted config. Clicking Save in that stale form re-creates the connection (upsert with the same id). Minor single-user edge. Fix: close/clear the form when the edited connection is removed (e.g. App reacts to the deleted id == editing.id and resets editing to undefined). Small UI polish, not blocking.
close_reason: Reactive guard closes the stale edit-form on delete; agent-reviewed LGTM, gates green, merged via PR #22.

title: Session-only / prompt-at-connect password (no Keychain persistence)
description: cwt.3 connection manager implements remember-password=true only (password -> Keychain via KeychainSecretStore). A session-only password (held in memory for the session, prompted at connect, never written to Keychain) is deferred. When wanted: add a session secret store (in-memory, app-lifetime) alongside KeychainSecretStore, and a 'remember password' unchecked path that prompts at connect/run. TODO(phase1) left in the connection form. Relates to PLAN.md §5 param-scope tiers conceptually but is simpler (just password lifetime).
close_reason: Session-only/prompt-at-connect password (PR #34). ConnectionConfig.remember_password flag; SessionOverlaySecretStore (ephemeral map over keychain-cache, clear_durable for on/off cleanup); set_session_password command; UI lock/unlock prompt. Secrets never on disk. Follow-up: billz-kub.

title: Bump frontend TypeScript 6 -> 7 once svelte-check validates the native compiler
description: Phase 1 scaffold (cwt.1) pins typescript@^6 (6.0.3, the last JS-based line) because TS 7.0.x is the new native/Go compiler and the JS tooling ecosystem (svelte-check 4, @tsconfig/svelte) isn't validated against it yet (create-tauri-app's own vanilla-ts template still pins TS ~6.0.3). When svelte-check ships a release that validates TS7, bump app/ui typescript to ^7 and re-run 'bun run check'. Does not affect vite build or cargo build; only the svelte-check type gate.
notes: FEASIBILITY (batch review): gated on ecosystem. package.json pins typescript 6 + svelte-check ^4.7.2; bump waits on svelte-check validating the TS 7 native (Go) compiler, which isn't confirmed available yet. Revisit when the toolchain supports it. Deferred.

title: Populate rows_affected for DML batches (executor sets None)
description: executor::run (ce1.6) sets QueryResult.rows_affected = None for every result set: the query_multiple/MultiResultStream path exposes no per-result DONE row counts (only the execute() path returns a u64, and it returns no rows). A pure-DML batch currently yields an empty Vec<QueryResult>. Populating affected-row counts for DML (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) needs a hybrid that also uses execute() or a driver enhancement. Deferred; TODO(later) in executor.rs. Not in ce1.6's AC.
notes: FEASIBILITY (billz-lpb-era batch review): BLOCKED on driver. The runner uses query_multiple → MultiResultStream, whose read path (mssql-client 0.20.2 client.rs:1277-1284) inspects Token::Done only for status.error/status.more and DISCARDS the DONE row count. rows_affected is exposed only on ExecuteResult (execute()) + bulk/procedure results — not on the multi-result path, and the runner can't route arbitrary batches to execute() (loses multi-result; can't know DML in advance; can't re-run). Unblock needs an upstream driver change: surface aggregate DONE rows_affected on MultiResultStream. Deferred until then; executor correctly sets None with a TODO pointer.

title: Capture PRINT/info messages from the driver (not exposed by mssql-client 0.20.2)
description: executor::run (ce1.6) returns Vec<QueryResult> with no messages channel: mssql-client 0.20.2's Token::Info (PRINT + informational messages) is only tracing::debug!'d (response.rs:271-277), never surfaced through a public API. Server ERRORs do surface (as CoreError::Query). PLAN.md §6 wants a messages pane showing PRINT/errors (Phase 1 cwt.7). Capturing PRINT would need a driver enhancement or a tracing-subscriber shim — deferred. A // TODO(later) is left in executor.rs. Re-check after any mssql-client bump.
notes: FEASIBILITY (batch review): BLOCKED on driver. mssql-client 0.20.2 exposes no info/message/print API on Client or the query streams — INFO tokens (PRINT output) are consumed internally and never surfaced. Needs an upstream driver change to expose a messages channel. Deferred.

title: bigint > 2^53 loses precision crossing JSON to the grid (CellValue::Int)
description: ce1.2's CellValue::Int(i64) serializes as a JSON number; JS JSON.parse reads it as f64, so |value| > 2^53 corrupts — the same precision-loss argument CLAUDE.md applies to decimals/money (which cross as strings). Follows PLAN.md §8's Int(i64) sketch, so not a spec violation, but a real hole for large bigint columns (snowflake IDs, hashes-as-bigint). Options: serialize Int as a string too, or a BigInt(String) variant for values outside the safe range. Low probability on personal DEV boxes; documented on CellValue::Int for now.
close_reason: bigint now crosses JSON as CellValue::BigInt(String); agent-reviewed LGTM, gates green, merged PR #23.

title: CellValue::Json + enable mssql-client 'json' feature (SQL Server 2025 native JSON)
description: ce1.2's CellValue has no Json variant: mssql-client's SqlValue::Json is behind the non-default 'json' feature (core uses default features), and native JSON is a SQL Server 2025+ type. On pre-2025 DEV boxes JSON is nvarchar(max) -> SqlValue::String -> CellValue::Text. When a 2025 box with native JSON is in scope: enable the mssql-client 'json' feature, add CellValue::Json(String), and add the ce1.6 SqlValue::Json mapping arm. Until then a Json variant would have no producer.
notes: FEASIBILITY (batch review): needs SQL Server 2025 (native JSON) + the mssql-client 'json' feature. DEV boxes aren't 2025; no server to validate against. Deferred until a 2025 box exists.

title: Width-aware friendly_type_name (IntN/FloatN/Money4/DateTime4 via max_length)
description: core::types::friendly_type_name (ce1.3) collapses nullable/narrow wire tokens to the common family: nullable bigint arrives as IntN(max_length=8) but maps to 'int'; FloatN len4 -> 'float' (should be 'real'); Money4/SmallMoney -> 'money'; DateTime4/smalldatetime -> 'datetime'. Correct disambiguation needs a second signature friendly_type_name_with_len(token, max_length). Deferred per PLAN.md §7 ('keep it simple, ignore token encoding for now'). Matters for the Phase 2 object tree's precise column types. A // TODO(phase2) marker is left at the IntN arm.
close_reason: Width-aware friendly_type_name via Column.max_length; widths verified against driver dispatch, agent-reviewed, gates green, merged PR #24.

title: Auto-type params from the catalog
description: When building a scoped query off a table, pre-fill param types from schema.rs (sys.columns + sys.types) — typed automatically from the schema, editable to override. Reuses the Phase 2 introspection layer. See PLAN.md section 5.
acceptance_criteria: Params built off a table column pre-fill their SQL type from the catalog and remain editable.
close_reason: Param type selector + catalogTypeToSqlType mapping shipped via PR #29. Design→plan-review→3 TDD tasks→code-review clean; verify green. Merged on user call (final review in-flight; strong green signals). Auto-fill trigger is d28.7.

title: Param scope tiers (Global < Session < Local)
description: Three tiers: Global defaults (@today) < Session values < per-query Local. Session scope = 'I'm on customer 12345 all afternoon' — set @cust once at session level; every saved query referencing it just works, no per-query prompting. See PLAN.md section 5.
acceptance_criteria: A session-level value satisfies all queries referencing that param without per-query prompts; Local overrides Session overrides Global.
close_reason: Param scope tiers (Session/Global stores, resolve precedence, scope selector, inherited badge) shipped via PR #28. Pipeline: mockup-approved → plan-review → 4 TDD tasks → code-review → final review READY TO MERGE (gates run live). gates green.

title: Explicit tree Refresh
description: Explicit Refresh action to invalidate the schema cache — I do DDL on DEV and want new objects immediately. See PLAN.md section 7.
acceptance_criteria: Refresh re-queries sys.* and shows newly created/dropped objects.
close_reason: Phase 2 Wave C merged in PR #15. Double-click table -> SELECT TOP 1000 tab (rqb.6), Refresh -> invalidate cache + remount tree (rqb.5), grey + disable non-ONLINE dbs (rqb.4). Agent gates green; live behavior is the user's tauri dev step.

title: Grey out non-ONLINE databases (state_desc)
description: Use state_desc from sys.databases to grey out non-ONLINE dbs; enumerating tables in a RESTORING/OFFLINE db errors on expand. See PLAN.md section 7.
acceptance_criteria: RESTORING/OFFLINE dbs render greyed and are not expandable/enumerated.
close_reason: Phase 2 Wave C merged in PR #15. Double-click table -> SELECT TOP 1000 tab (rqb.6), Refresh -> invalidate cache + remount tree (rqb.5), grey + disable non-ONLINE dbs (rqb.4). Agent gates green; live behavior is the user's tauri dev step.

title: object_name ignores <Object @Server>, collapsing linked-server objects onto local ones
description:
core/src/plan/parse.rs object_name builds from ["Database","Schema","Table","Index"] and ignores the Server attribute that ShowPlanXML emits for an object on a linked server. Two consequences: a finding's evidence cannot distinguish a linked-server object from a same-named local one, and after fingerprint::strip_database the two collapse to the same token in the shape key, so a plan that reaches out to a linked server would be grouped with one that stays local.

Not reachable from anything this project does today - no query it issues touches a linked server, and no captured fixture contains an Object with a Server attribute. Raised by the independent code review of billz-xi6.3 because it is adjacent to strip_database.

If ever fixed: add Server to the front of object_name's list, and note that strip_database's leading-component cut would then need to account for a four-or-five component name.

title: Decide whether PlanNode should carry NodeId
description:
ShowPlanXML RelOp elements carry a NodeId attribute that PlanNode currently drops. Nothing needs it today, but it is what makes a plan operator ADDRESSABLE: a UI that highlights or links to a specific operator needs it, and tests that want to pin a tree path exactly must currently approximate with a physical-op sequence (see discovers_children_through_wrappers_in_a_deep_tree in parse.rs, which asserts a 20-element PhysicalOp path plus two subtree costs to disambiguate two identically-named siblings - a NodeId path would have been exact).

Cheap to add (one attribute read, one field, one line in the camelCase round-trip test). Raised by the billz-xi6.2 author so it is a decision rather than an omission. Revisit when Unit 6 builds the operator tree-table.

title: core/Cargo.toml lists serde_json in both [dependencies] and [dev-dependencies]
description: The dev-dependencies entry is redundant - serde_json is already a normal dependency, so it is available to tests regardless. Harmless and pre-existing; found during billz-xi6.1 implementation. Remove the duplicate line.

title: Stale comment: core/tests/dev_box.rs env_connection() points at the wrong file
description: core/tests/dev_box.rs:32 has its own env_connection() copy whose doc comment says it mirrors the private helper in executor.rs. That helper moved to test_support.rs (billz-2co), and an integration-test crate cannot see #[cfg(test)] items anyway, so the duplication is structural and correct - only the comment is wrong. Found during billz-xi6.1 implementation. Comment fix only, no behaviour change.

title: Graphical execution-plan view (optional, time-boxed)
description: Priced at roughly 1-2 focused days ON TOP OF the core::plan parse that the verdict already requires - the cost was never the picture, it was the parse. Tree layout is about 100 lines (depth to column, subtree extent to row); connecting lines are SVG paths with thickness from estimated rows; colour-code the eight operator classes that matter instead of sourcing ~70 icons. DO NOT port html-query-plan: MIT but last committed ~5 years ago, it is an XSLT 1.0 stylesheet (XSLTProcessor in the webview is a CSP risk - note app.security.csp applies only to the packaged build, not just dev), it needs a ~70-icon set of uncertain provenance, and it would re-parse in JavaScript what core parses in Rust. No maintained alternative exists (azdataGraph is a derivative of the discontinued mxGraph and is a general diagramming component). Decide only AFTER using the operator tree-table; the surviving argument against is that a graph does not compose with fan-out - 27 plan trees is not an interface. Time-box it: pan, zoom and icon fidelity are where scope creep lives.

title: Gitignore .playwright-mcp/ and stray screenshot artifacts
description:
Found during the billz-667/billz-1kn agent-team run.

The Playwright MCP server writes screenshots and a .playwright-mcp/ directory into the REPO ROOT and refuses to write outside the repo, so they cannot be routed to a scratchpad. Neither is gitignored, so every visual-verification pass leaves untracked junk that a careless 'git add -A' would sweep into a feature commit. This has now happened across four separate units; each time it was avoided only because authors were explicitly told to stage paths by name.

Add .playwright-mcp/ and a screenshot pattern to .gitignore so the safety does not depend on every future agent remembering.
acceptance_criteria: A visual-verification pass leaves no untracked files visible in git status. .playwright-mcp/ is ignored.

title: Audit window.confirm usage the way window.prompt was
description:
Found by plan review on billz-1kn.

NameDialog.svelte documents that window.prompt is unreliable in the Tauri v2 WKWebView, which is why name entry is an inline modal. But SavedQueryLibrary.svelte still deletes behind window.confirm, and that call was never audited against the same concern.

Either confirm that window.confirm IS reliable in this webview and record that finding next to the prompt comment, or replace it with an inline confirm dialog. Right now the codebase asserts one native dialog is unreliable while depending on a sibling one.
acceptance_criteria: window.confirm usage is either justified with a recorded finding or replaced. The prompt/confirm reasoning is consistent.
close_reason: Resolved by PR #81. Verified on merged main: zero window.confirm/window.prompt CALLS remain under app/ui/src — all remaining textual hits are comments explaining why the native dialogs went. The prompt/confirm reasoning now lives in one place, ConfirmDialog.svelte's header.

title: pushToast arms a timer for a toast that addToast just evicted
description:
Found by plan review on billz-667. Pre-existing, latent, not made worse by that unit.

toasts.svelte.ts pushToast arms its setTimeout keyed on the newly minted id unconditionally, without checking whether addToast evicted that very toast on the way in. Reachable only when maxTransient is small enough that the incoming transient is itself the oldest transient and gets evicted immediately — no production caller does this (MAX_VISIBLE is 4); toastLogic.test.ts exercises the cap-0 path for stickies only.

Effect today is benign: an orphan timeout fires later and calls dismiss() on an id that is not in the stack, which is a no-op. Worth closing anyway because the whole timer design in this module is built on the invariant that no timer outlives its toast, and this is the one place that invariant is not actually enforced.
acceptance_criteria: pushToast does not arm a timer for a toast that was evicted during the same call. Covered by a test that drives the eviction-on-insert path.

title: Toast overflow counter counts entries, not occurrences
description:
Found by plan review on billz-667 (toast coalescing). Cosmetic follow-on that coalescing creates.

ToastHost's hiddenLabel builds the '+N earlier errors' chip by counting collapsed toast ENTRIES. Once repeated identical messages coalesce into one entry carrying a repeat count, a collapsed entry with repeat>1 makes that chip UNDERCOUNT the actual number of error occurrences: three collapsed entries where one has repeat 5 reads '+3 earlier errors' for 7 real failures.

Arguably correct as-is — the chip describes how many rows are hidden, which is what expanding reveals. But it is a new discrepancy introduced by coalescing, and 'how many errors happened' is the question a user is actually asking of that number. Decide which it means and make the label say so.
acceptance_criteria: The overflow chip's number is unambiguous about whether it counts hidden rows or total occurrences, and the label wording matches.

title: Evaluate switching driver to microsoft/mssql-rs (mssql-tds) once stable
description:
Tracking item (not actionable yet). Microsoft is building an official Rust TDS driver at github.com/microsoft/mssql-rs (core crate: mssql-tds). Steve wants to migrate core's driver from mssql-client (0.20.x) to it ONCE STABLE, since an official MS-backed driver is a stronger long-term bet than the current single-maintainer crate.

As of 2026-07-17 it is NOT ready: no releases, not published to crates.io, internal-dev only (no external PRs), no stability/versioning guarantees. Do not switch yet.

Switch criteria — re-evaluate when ALL hold:
- Published to crates.io with a real (>=0.x tagged) release + changelog.
- rustls TLS support (repo invariant: TLS=rustls, no native-tls).
- SQL-auth (user/pass) connection support (we only need SQL auth, no Entra/AAD).
- Connection pooling or an equivalent we can wrap.
- Type coverage for what core needs: decimals/money (string across JSON boundary), UUID, datetime/chrono, plus the wire-token vs canonical-type metadata split (PLAN.md §7).

Migration is bounded by design: driver stays private to core (CLAUDE.md invariant), so this is a core-only change. Touch sites: core/src/{connection,executor,query,result,types,param_bind,schema,session,error}.rs. Re-run the spike integration tests (core/tests/dev_box.rs, gated on MSSQL_* env) against the new driver before trusting it. NOTE: mssql-client is open source and forkable — do NOT trade it for anything closed-source (ruled out SeaORM X / SQLz commercial driver on 2026-07-17).

Ref: https://github.com/microsoft/mssql-rs
notes: Decided 2026-07-17: no switch to SeaORM (SQL Server support = commercial closed-source SeaORM X + ORM paradigm mismatch). Track microsoft/mssql-rs instead.

title: Object tree: right-click / double-click table doesn't move selection highlight
description: Follow-up flagged during billz-a8a plan review. Selection (billz-a8a) is click/Enter-driven; TableNode's oncontextmenu (scoped-query menu) and ondblclick (openSelect / SELECT TOP 1000) fire their actions without calling selectNode, so opening a query from the tree leaves the highlight on the previously-selected row. Within the a8a spec, but a minor UX inconsistency: consider calling selectNode(key) from those handlers too.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #59: DatabaseNode/TableNode rows expose aria-expanded (offline DB omits it as non-expandable); TableNode right-click (openMenu) now moves the selection highlight via selectNode. Gates green, final review PASS, behavior verified via Playwright DOM/a11y drive.

title: Object tree: expand/collapse rows lack aria-expanded
description: Follow-up flagged during billz-a8a final review. DatabaseNode/TableNode rows are <button>s that toggle expand/collapse but expose no aria-expanded state, so screen readers get no cue about expanded vs collapsed. Pre-existing (predates a8a). Add aria-expanded bound to the node's expanded state. Low priority, single-user tool.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #59: DatabaseNode/TableNode rows expose aria-expanded (offline DB omits it as non-expandable); TableNode right-click (openMenu) now moves the selection highlight via selectNode. Gates green, final review PASS, behavior verified via Playwright DOM/a11y drive.

title: Fan-out DB selection is not scoped per connection (selection pruned on connection-switch + edit)
description: Latent footgun flagged by author-ui + code-reviewer-ui-r1 during PR#2. A tab's fanoutDatabases is a single per-tab list; effectiveFanoutDatabases prunes it to the current connection's ONLINE DBs. If you switch the tab to a different connection and then edit the picker, the prior connection's selection is silently dropped (rebuilt from the pruned effFanoutDbs). Consistent with the existing single-DB database/effectiveDb pattern (never target an absent DB), so acceptable for now — but 'selection lost on connection switch + edit' is surprising. Fix would need per-connection selection retention (picker keeps out-of-store names). Deferred.

title: CachingSecretStore: single-flight get_password to avoid Keychain thundering-herd under parallel connects
description: Pre-existing (NOT introduced by fan-out): CachingSecretStore::get_password (connection.rs:261) checks the cache, releases the lock, calls the inner Keychain store, then re-locks to insert — lock not held across the inner call. So N parallel connects for the same connection id on a cold cache all miss and all hit the Keychain concurrently. run_fanout is just the first parallel caller to make it observable. Harmless for a single-user app with Keychain access already granted (no prompt). Fix = single-flight/coalescing in CachingSecretStore, if ever wanted. Flagged by author-backend + code-reviewer during fan-out PR#1.

title: Prune unbounded columnWidths localStorage store (follow-up to billz-389)
description: billz-389 persists result-grid column widths in localStorage key billz.columnWidths.v1, keyed by column-name signature (JSON.stringify of ordered names). Every distinct result shape adds a signature entry forever — the store grows unbounded across sessions with no eviction. Fine for a single-user 'good enough' tool now (flagged during the billz-389 plan review), but worth a bounded LRU / size cap or a periodic prune eventually. Mirror the quiet-degrade pattern in columnWidths.svelte.ts / globalParams.svelte.ts. Deferred per scope discipline.
close_reason: Bounded columnWidths localStorage store: MAX_WIDTH_SIGNATURES=100 cap with touch-on-write LRU eviction (delete-then-reinsert to most-recent tail, evict oldest past cap) + cap-on-load self-heal for pre-fix bloat. Pure evictSignatures helper in columnWidthsLogic.ts with 7 unit tests.

title: VPN preflight: reachability check before connect (no embedded VPN)
description:
Make billz fail helpfully when the VPN tunnel to the SQL Server DEV box is down, WITHOUT embedding a VPN stack. Do NOT build yet.

Context: main SQL Server use requires Azure VPN with MS Entra-backed auth, imported via XML profile.

Explicitly NOT building an embedded VPN: that means IKEv2/OpenVPN + XML-profile parsing + Entra interactive OAuth/SAML (browser round-trip, not headless) + a macOS Network Extension entitlement (requires a paid Apple Developer account and Apple's manual capability approval — well past the current self-signed setup in SIGNING.md). Effort is wildly out of proportion for a single-user tool.

What to build instead (the useful 90%):
- Reachability preflight (trivial): before connect, TCP-probe server host:port; on failure show 'VPN appears down — bring up your tunnel and retry' rather than a cryptic driver timeout. A few lines in the connect path.
- Optional, later: shell out to a configured macOS VPN service (scutil --nc start/status '<name>') to kick off the tunnel. Caveat: Azure VPN + Entra interactive auth still pops a browser to finish auth — cannot be fully automated.

Estimated gnarliness: preflight is trivial-small; embedded VPN is out of scope. From a 2026-07-13 feasibility discussion.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #51 (VPN reachability preflight)

title: DuckDB backend: SQLite + Parquet/CSV via one embedded engine
description:
Add a second executor backend behind core's driver seam so billz can open SQLite files and query Parquet/CSV — a deliberate scope expansion beyond the SQL-Server-only charter (CLAUDE.md), tracked so it isn't lost. Do NOT build yet.

Why DuckDB: one embedded engine (duckdb crate, no server) speaks real SQL, reads Parquet/CSV natively (SELECT * FROM 'f.parquet'), and can ATTACH SQLite files — collapsing 'other SQL DBs' and 'data-science file types' into a single backend.

Feasibility (grounded in current core/):
- The value boundary is already backend-agnostic: CellValue/QueryResult/ColumnMeta (result.rs) carry zero mssql_client types and the grid renders them as-is. The string-encoded Decimal/BigInt anti-f64-precision rule maps cleanly to DuckDB DECIMAL128.
- Real work: (1) introduce a Backend trait and make executor.rs's run/run_with_params the SQL Server impl, add a DuckDB impl; (2) fork schema.rs introspection — it is hardwired to sys.* T-SQL; DuckDB uses information_schema (closer to portable than sqlite_master/PRAGMA); (3) connection model shift — file path, no server/port, no Keychain password (the secrets-never-touch-disk invariant simply doesn't apply); (4) ExecutionContext { database } generalizes (file / ATTACHed schema).
- Known gap: nested types (LIST/STRUCT, nested Parquet). Launch scalar-only; add a JSON-ish CellValue variant later.

Estimated gnarliness: moderate. The core boundary permits this cleanly; schema.rs's dialect fork is the sharp edge. From a 2026-07-13 feasibility discussion.

title: Flipping remember-off→on without retyping password leaves no Keychain entry
description: 85b final-review nit 2. When editing a session-only connection to remember-on WITHOUT retyping the password (password=None), save_connection's remember-on branch writes nothing to the Keychain (None = no change). It works the rest of the session via the retained session-map entry, but after restart the connection is remember-on with no stored secret AND remember-on connections don't get the unlock prompt (only session-only ones lock), so the next op fails with Config("no stored password") and the only recovery is to edit + retype. Options: on off→on flip require a (re)typed password; or if flipping to on with a live session password, promote it to the Keychain; or surface a hint. Low priority — an edge of the edit flow.
acceptance_criteria: Flipping a connection to remember-on results in a durable Keychain password (or the UI prevents/─explains the no-password state); no silent post-restart failure.
close_reason: Promote the session password to the Keychain on remember-off→on flip (PR #37). save_connection persists the known session password when flipping to remember-on with no retype, so it survives restart. Only on the flip (no redundant Keychain writes).

title: Add a way to clear/reset a param's Session/Global tier value
description: d28.4 plan-review gap: routeWrites/setSessionParams/setGlobalParams only ever WRITE tier values; there's no in-app path to clear one. Consequences: (1) a Global default persists in localStorage forever; (2) setting a Global value while a Session value for that name is active is shadowed (Session > Global by design) with no way to clear the Session value except app restart. Both are correct per the §5 precedence model but leave stale values unremovable in-app. Add a clear/reset affordance (e.g. an 'x' on the scope control, or a session/global params manager) once the tier UX matures. Deferred from d28.4.
acceptance_criteria: User can clear a param's Session and Global value from the UI; a cleared Global value is removed from localStorage.
close_reason: Clear tier value via badge × (PR #33). clearSessionParam/clearGlobalParam (Global removed from localStorage); onClearTier clears + refreshes field via resolve. Badge × on surfaced tier; chaining clears both. Closes the d28 epic.

title: Consolidate duplicated env_connection() test helper across core modules
description: env_connection() (builds a live ConnectionConfig+store from MSSQL_* or None) is copy-pasted in executor.rs, schema.rs, and session.rs test modules (and a variant in app/src/lib.rs). A ConnectionConfig field change means editing each copy (compile error if one is missed — loud, not silent). Extract one shared #[cfg(test)] test-support helper in core (pub(crate) fn behind cfg(test)) for the three in-crate copies. title: Schema cache can re-cache stale rows if a connection is edited mid-fetch
description: Race surfaced by billz-lpb high code-review: forget_connection (on save/delete) clears the schema cache + evicts the session, but an in-flight list_* holds a clone of the old Slot Arc and keeps querying the OLD server; when it returns, get_or_fetch re-inserts the pre-edit rows into the cleared cache, so the tree shows stale schema until a manual Refresh. Rare on a single-user tool (requires editing a connection's server/creds while a subtree expand is mid-flight). Correct fix needs a generation counter / cache-write guard keyed to the pre-edit epoch. Deferred from the billz-lpb review (out of that diff's scope).
acceptance_criteria: Editing a connection while an expand is in flight cannot leave pre-edit schema cached; the stale in-flight result is discarded.
close_reason: Schema-cache generation guard (PR #38). get_or_fetch stamps a global AtomicU64 generation, re-checks under the insert lock; clears bump before clearing. A mid-fetch edit/Refresh can no longer re-cache stale rows; in-flight result returned uncached. Airtight per plan-review.

title: Tolerate omitted Option fields in hand-edited config/query JSON
description: Both ConnectionStore (connections.json) and QueryStore (saved_queries.json) deserialize Option fields WITHOUT #[serde(default)]: connection.rs default_database; query.rs target_database, Param.sql_type, Param.last_value. In serde a MISSING key on a plain Option<T> field is a deserialize ERROR, not None — so a human hand-editing the JSON and omitting one of these keys makes the whole file fail to load (surfaces as CoreError::Store 'missing field'). Machine round-trips are unaffected (serialize always writes every key incl. null), so this is latent, not a live bug. query.rs's module doc even states the intent: 'serde(default) on defaulted fields so a hand-edited JSON file loads cleanly' — currently honored for params/scope but not the Option fields. FIX (a consistency pass across BOTH files, not one wave): add #[serde(default)] to those Option fields so an omitted key loads as None. Deliberately NOT done in d28.1 because query.rs mirrors the merged connection.rs precedent, which also omits it — diverging one store from the other would be worse than the gap. Do both together.
close_reason: Already satisfied — serde_derive defaults missing Option<T> fields to None (no serde(default) needed for Option; only non-Option). Bead premise (missing key → error) was incorrect. Added regression tests (PR #35) pinning the hand-edited-loads-cleanly behavior; no source fix required.
